text: NotebookLM - Composio Toolkit | Composio All Toolkits NotebookLM NOTEBOOK_LM Latest version 20261101_00 NotebookLM Enterprise is Google's licensed, source-grounded notebook service for organizing sources in global-location deployments. Copy page Authentication Details Composio-managed OAuth available OAuth2 Frequently Asked Questions How do I set up custom Google OAuth credentials for NotebookLM? Use your own Google OAuth app when you want your app name on the consent screen, your own API quota, or full control over the requested scopes. NotebookLM connects to an existing Gemini Notebook Enterprise deployment in the Global location. The user needs an active license and the Cloud NotebookLM User role in the deployment project. See Google's Notebook Enterprise API prerequisites . Create the Google OAuth app In Google Cloud Console , select the project that will own the OAuth client, or create one. Open APIs & Services → Library , search for Discovery Engine API ( discoveryengine.googleapis.com ), and select Enable . If the page shows Manage , the API is already enabled. Enable it in the project that hosts your Notebook Enterprise deployment. Open Google Auth Platform → Branding . If Google shows Get started , enter the app name, user support email, and developer contact email, then save. Open Audience . Choose Internal to limit the app to users in your Google Workspace organization, or External for consumer accounts and users outside it. While an external app's publishing status is Testing , only accounts listed under Test users can connect, so add every account you'll test with. Open Data Access → Add or remove scopes and add the scopes listed under Scopes below. If a scope isn't in the list, paste its full URL under Manually add scopes and select Add to table . Select Update , then Save . Open Clients → Create client , choose Web application , and give it a name. Under Authorized redirect URIs , add https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add . It must exactly match the oauth_redirect_uri field on your Composio auth config. Select Create . Copy the Client ID and Client secret . Google shows the full secret only once, so save it before you close the dialog. Create the auth config in Composio In the Composio dashboard , open Auth Configs → Create and select NotebookLM . Choose OAuth 2.0 and Your Own Credentials , then paste your Client ID and Client secret . Leave Redirect URI unchanged, keep the scopes in line with what you added in Google, and select Create Auth Config . Open the auth config, select Connect Account , and enter the Google Cloud project ID or numeric project number that hosts the Notebook Enterprise deployment. Then sign in. If the connection fails, check the Global location, the user's license, the Discovery Engine API, and IAM access in that project. Open Accounts on the auth config and confirm the connected account shows Active . The auth config's own Enabled label doesn't confirm a connection. For the general flow, see Custom auth configs . Scopes The default auth config requests https://www.googleapis.com/auth/discoveryengine.readwrite . It can authorize Discovery Engine writes within the user's IAM permissions. See the notebook listing reference for the required scopes and IAM permissions. Short scope names on this page leave out the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/ prefix. When you paste a scope under Manually add scopes , use the full URL, for example https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email . Scopes already written as a full URL, such as https://mail.google.com/ , go in as shown. Publish and verify the app While an external app is in Testing , Google shows an unverified-app notice and refresh tokens expire after seven days, so users have to reconnect. Before you invite production users, select Publish app on the Audience page. A public app that requests sensitive or restricted scopes also needs Google's OAuth verification, which you start from Verification Center . Publishing doesn't complete verification on its own. Internal apps and apps in Testing can be exempt. See Google's verification requirements . If you change the requested scopes later, reconnect the account so the user grants the new access.
